instrument: xml own-file preference — the fix for the `calls` 138, measured with a toggle control
population: libxslt, 1,143 files indexed, ONE RUN PER ARM. Every arm below is the same population and the same instrument; the only thing that differs is stated per arm.

theDefect.what: Both lookup tables collapse EVERY name and every dotted suffix to ONE global winner via `MIN(id)` — the lexicographically smallest symbol id in the PROJECT. File paths sort, so an edge written in `tests/docbook/html/admon.xsl` binds to the same-named template declared in the PARALLEL tree `tests/docbook/fo/admon.xsl` (`fo` < `html`). Strategy 1's `_res_qname` does the same for exact qualified names, which is why `colspec.colnum` bound to an attribute symbol in `tests/docbook/test/article2.xml`.
theDefect.hypothesisRefutedOnTheWay: The first reading was the INSERT-time statement (`resolveTargetStmt`) preferring `COALESCE(is_declaration,0)` over own-file. A kept store REFUTED it: for `admon.graphic.width` both candidates are tier 0 and the own file wins that statement — yet the row was bound to `fo/`. The pass, not the insert, was binding them. Recorded because the wrong site would have produced a fix that could not work.

theFix.shape: three own-file passes that run BEFORE the project-wide statements, which are untouched and still fire for every row they fired for before (they require `target_symbol_id IS NULL`): (1) own-file exact qualified-name match, (2) own-file NAME match, (3) own-file dotted-suffix match. Each binds only when the edge's target is declared in the edge's OWN file, and sets `is_cross_file = 0`.
theFix.author: designed and measured by this lane; landed inside another lane's commit — see landedIn
patches: validation/m14/fixtures/xml/own-file-preference-armB.patch (arm B: + own-file NAME, 138 -> 0; this is what landed)
theFix.landedIn: 63a888b03 (23:40:24) — another lane's commit for its `extractLeaf` path fix swept this lane's uncommitted in-flight edits into the same commit. The patch is therefore IN HEAD, not handed over. This lane did not commit it, and reports the sweep as a process finding: the Lead's exact-path commit rule exists for this.

toggleControl.note: THE DECISIVE ARM. Same tree (current HEAD, which contains both the extractLeaf fix and the own-file passes), same population, one run each; the ONLY change is the three own-file UPDATEs neutered with `WHERE 0 AND`.
toggleControl.reading: The three own-file passes account for the ENTIRE reduction on this population: 147 -> 4, calls 138 -> 0. The extractLeaf fix does not move these counts.

regressionCheck.condition: the `builtin` / `external` / `unresolved` / `file` classes bind elsewhere CORRECTLY and are never scored, so any movement there is a regression.
regressionCheck.result: 0 of those classes moved in the toggle control.
regressionCheck.contains: every axis improves, none worsens: intended 16,106 -> 17,625 (+1,519), arbitraryTwin 3,393 -> 2,296 (-1,097), unbound 1,802 -> 13 (-1,789). The newly bound rows are containment edges whose target IS declared in their own file and which the eager contains path had left unbound.

theRemaining4.imports3: `xml-stylesheet` -> `#style1` / `#transform` in libxslt/tests/REC/stand-2.7-*.xml — document-internal ID references, class `in-document` with NO own-file declaration of that name (`declaredInSourceFile` empty). Nothing for a name-based resolver to prefer; the store leaves them unbound, which is arguably the right shape, and the analyzer's class is what is loose here.
theRemaining4.references1: one edge with an EMPTY source spelling and the target `target`, bound to XSLTMark/tower.xsl:12, class `in-document`, no own-file declaration. An outlier rather than the same mechanism.
theRemaining4.whyTheFixCannotReachThem: own-file preference needs an own-file declaration to prefer; for these 4 there is none. They are a different question (the analyzer's class), not a resolver question.
